purpose: Hallucination-prevention eval set for X3 Compass FMCSA skill builders. Every skill-builder agent must pass >= 95% before its PR can be merged. CFR text round-trips against eCFR API (ecfr.federalregister.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/...).

scoring.method: Each Q is scored 0 or 1. Pass if (a) answer cites the listed citation (or all listed if multiple), and (b) any quoted regulation text is an exact substring of live eCFR text. Paraphrase OK. Made-up citations or quotes = 0. Common_hallucinations are explicit fail-traps — if answer matches one of them, hard 0.

questions.question: What documents must be retained in a driver's qualification file for the duration of employment plus three years after termination?
common_hallucinations: citing 391.21 (which is just the application form, not the file contents)

questions.question: How long must a motor carrier retain the application for employment after a driver leaves?
What inquiries must a motor carrier make about a prospective driver's previous employment?
key_concepts: drug and alcohol testing history per Part 40

questions.question: What is required for a driver to be qualified to operate a CMV under Part 391?
common_hallucinations: claiming 18 years old (that's intrastate in some states, NOT 391.11)

questions.question: What is the road test requirement and what is an acceptable substitute?
key_concepts: carrier may accept valid CDL as equivalent except for double/triple trailers and tank vehicles
common_hallucinations: claiming CDL always substitutes (it doesn't for doubles/triples/tanks)

questions.question: What is the maximum driving time for a property-carrying driver between off-duty periods?
What is the 60/70-hour limit and when does the 34-hour restart apply?
key_concepts: 60 hours in 7 consecutive days (carriers not operating every day of the week)
70 hours in 8 consecutive days (carriers operating every day)
34 consecutive hours off duty to restart
common_hallucinations: claiming the restart must include two 1am-5am periods (that requirement was rescinded)

questions.question: What is the 30-minute rest break requirement under HOS rules?
key_concepts: 30 minutes interrupting any 8 cumulative hours of driving time
can be satisfied by on-duty not-driving status (as of 2020 amendment)
common_hallucinations: claiming it must be off-duty (the 2020 amendment allows on-duty not-driving)
saying it's every 8 hours of on-duty time

questions.question: What is the sleeper berth split provision currently allowed?
key_concepts: one period in sleeper at least 7 consecutive hours
second period at least 2 consecutive hours either in sleeper or off-duty
neither period counts against the 14-hour window
common_hallucinations: claiming only 8/2 is allowed (7/3 is also allowed since 2020)
claiming the second period must be in the sleeper berth

questions.question: When is the short-haul exception available and what are its limits?
key_concepts: return to work-reporting location within 14 hours
records kept by employer for 6 months
common_hallucinations: claiming 100 air-mile (that was the old limit before 2020)

questions.question: When is a post-accident drug and alcohol test required?
key_concepts: citation issued + bodily injury treated away from scene
citation issued + disabling damage requiring tow-away
common_hallucinations: claiming all accidents trigger a test

questions.question: What categories of testing does Part 382 require?
What is the minimum annual random testing rate for controlled substances under Part 382?
key_concepts: 50% of average number of driver positions for controlled substances
rate set by FMCSA Administrator annually
based on positive rate from prior year
common_hallucinations: claiming the rate is fixed forever

questions.question: What must a motor carrier do upon receiving a Clearinghouse query showing a violation?
key_concepts: cannot return to safety-sensitive function until completing return-to-duty process
common_hallucinations: claiming the carrier can immediately retest in-house

questions.question: Who is the Designated Employer Representative (DER) and what is their authority?
key_concepts: cannot be a service agent (C/TPA staff)
common_hallucinations: claiming the MRO is the DER
claiming the C/TPA can be the DER

questions.question: How long is a standard CDL driver medical examiner's certificate valid?
key_concepts: shorter at examiner's discretion based on health
must be issued by certified medical examiner on National Registry

questions.question: What is required for a driver with insulin-treated diabetes mellitus (ITDM) to qualify?
key_concepts: no waiver required as of 2018 rule

questions.question: What vision standard must a driver meet under Part 391?
key_concepts: distant visual acuity 20/40 each eye with or without correction
field of vision 70 degrees in horizontal meridian each eye
ability to recognize colors of traffic signals and devices
common_hallucinations: forgetting the field of vision requirement

questions.question: What hearing standard must a driver meet?
key_concepts: forced whisper at 5 feet with or without hearing aid
OR average hearing loss not exceeding 40 dB at 500/1000/2000 Hz with or without hearing aid
common_hallucinations: forgetting the 'or' between the two tests

questions.question: What blood pressure standards apply to medical certification?
questions.citation: FMCSA Medical Examiner Handbook + 391.41 advisory criteria
key_concepts: Stage 2 (160-179/100-109): one-time 3-month cert then annual if controlled
not a strict 391.41 numeric standard but FMCSA advisory criteria
common_hallucinations: citing 391.41 as having explicit BP numbers (it doesn't — the handbook does)

questions.question: How long must a motor carrier retain annual inspection reports for each vehicle?
key_concepts: kept at location specified by carrier

questions.question: What constitutes a Driver Vehicle Inspection Report (DVIR) requirement?
key_concepts: written or electronic report at end of each work day
only required if defect or deficiency that affects safe operation
carrier must repair or determine no repair needed
common_hallucinations: claiming DVIR required every day even with no defects (rescinded 2014)

questions.question: What is the brake performance requirement under Part 393?
key_concepts: service brake stopping distance: 35 mph initial speed
specific stopping distances by vehicle type
common_hallucinations: confusing service vs emergency brake distances

questions.question: What pre-trip inspection items are required under 392.7?
common_hallucinations: claiming a specific time duration (392.7 doesn't dictate one)

questions.question: How long must DVIRs be retained?
What is the placard threshold for Table 2 hazardous materials being transported by highway?
key_concepts: Table 1 materials placard regardless of quantity

questions.question: What materials are in Table 1 (placard at any quantity)?
key_concepts: Class 2.3 Inhalation Hazard Zone A or B
Class 6.1 PG I Inhalation Hazard Zone A
common_hallucinations: putting Class 3 flammable liquids in Table 1

questions.question: What documentation must accompany a hazmat shipment by highway?
common_hallucinations: forgetting the emergency response phone number

questions.question: What hazmat training is required for hazmat employees under Part 172 Subpart H?
key_concepts: in-depth security training (if HM security plan required)

questions.question: What is the HM-181 hazardous materials registration requirement?
key_concepts: required for offerors and carriers of certain hazmat
common_hallucinations: confusing with the FMCSA Hazmat Safety Permit at 385 Subpart E (separate program)

questions.question: Which BASIC categories does FMCSA's Safety Measurement System (SMS) currently use?
questions.note: BASIC percentiles are NOT public via free FMCSA API since 2015 FAST Act.

questions.question: How long do roadside inspection violations stay in the SMS calculation?
key_concepts: time-weighted: violations in months 0-6 weighted 3, months 7-12 weighted 2, months 13-24 weighted 1

questions.question: What is the Inspection Selection System (ISS) score and how is it used?
key_concepts: calculated from CSA BASIC percentiles + inspection history
common_hallucinations: claiming roadside officers see the BASIC percentiles directly (they see ISS, derived from BASICs)

questions.question: What is a DataQ challenge and what kinds of records can be challenged?
questions.citation: FMCSA DataQ — Request for Data Review
common_hallucinations: claiming state law violations can be challenged via DataQ (state DOT handles those)
claiming citations are challenged via DataQ (those go through traffic court)

questions.question: What is the Crash Preventability Determination Program?
key_concepts: determination as 'not preventable' removes crash from Crash Indicator BASIC SMS calculation
does not remove crash from public Carrier Profile (CSA) record
common_hallucinations: claiming preventability removes crash from all FMCSA records (it only affects Crash Indicator)

questions.question: How often must a motor carrier obtain a Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) for each driver?
key_concepts: from each state where driver held a CDL during the year

questions.question: What must a motor carrier do based on the annual MVR review?
key_concepts: note any violations affecting CMV operation
common_hallucinations: claiming no documentation needed if MVR is clean

questions.question: What is the driver's obligation to report convictions under 391.27?
key_concepts: list of violations of motor vehicle laws
common_hallucinations: claiming only CMV-related violations need reporting (it's all violations except parking)

questions.question: What is the CDL holder's obligation to notify employer of conviction?
key_concepts: any violation of state/local law relating to motor vehicle traffic
contains specific elements (location, court, plea, etc.)
common_hallucinations: forgetting it applies to all states not just home state

questions.question: What is the CDL holder's obligation to notify their employer of license suspension/revocation/cancellation?
key_concepts: by end of business day following day driver received notice

questions.question: What is the minimum public liability insurance amount required for a for-hire motor carrier transporting non-hazardous freight?
What is the minimum insurance for a for-hire carrier transporting oil listed in 49 CFR 172.101 (hazardous materials, Class 3)?
What is the minimum insurance for carriers of certain extremely hazardous materials (e.g., poisonous gases, certain bulk materials)?
How long must a motor carrier retain accident registers under 390.15?
What is the duration that a motor carrier must retain driver inspection records and other Part 379 records?
key_concepts: drug tests per 382.401: 1-5 years depending on result type
common_hallucinations: claiming a single retention period for all records

questions.question: What is the weight threshold (GVWR or GVW) above which a vehicle is considered a commercial motor vehicle (CMV) under Part 390?
key_concepts: GVWR or GVW of 10,001 pounds or more
designed/used to transport 9+ passengers including driver for compensation
any quantity of hazmat requiring placards

questions.question: What is the CDL weight threshold under Part 383?
key_concepts: Class C: vehicle not meeting A or B but designed for 16+ passengers or hazmat placards
common_hallucinations: confusing with the CMV definition in 390.5

questions.question: What is the difference between intrastate and interstate motor-carrier authority?
key_concepts: interstate: crossing state lines or transporting goods that will (or have)
interstate CMV operations subject to all FMCSRs
intrastate operations subject to state rules but FMCSA does require CDL standards for intrastate CMVs over 26k
common_hallucinations: claiming intrastate is exempt from CDL Part 383

questions.question: What is the FMCSA New Entrant Safety Audit requirement?
key_concepts: safety audit must be completed within first 12 months of operations
failure to comply results in revocation of new entrant registration
specific automatic failure violations listed in 385.321

questions.question: What is the difference between a Compliance Review and a Safety Audit?
key_concepts: Compliance Review: comprehensive examination leading to safety rating (Satisfactory/Conditional/Unsatisfactory)
Safety Audit: new entrant audit, no rating issued, pass/fail
CR can be triggered by SMS data, complaints, crashes; Safety Audit is the new-entrant program
common_hallucinations: claiming a safety audit produces a Conditional rating

questions.question: Who is required to use an ELD?
key_concepts: exemptions: short-haul (150 air-mile), driveaway-tow, pre-2000 model year truck, ≤8 days of RODS in any 30-day period
common_hallucinations: claiming all CMV drivers must use ELDs

questions.question: What duty status changes must an ELD automatically record?
key_concepts: on-duty driving when vehicle moves at >5 mph
duty status change at engine start/stop with prompt
yard moves and personal conveyance must be manually selected
automatic transition to on-duty driving after 5 minutes stopped if no input
common_hallucinations: claiming all 4 duty statuses change automatically (only driving auto-engages)

questions.question: How long must ELD data be retained?
key_concepts: data backed up at least monthly

questions.question: What must a driver do during a roadside inspection regarding ELD records?
key_concepts: via display, printout, telematic transfer, or local transfer
driver retains last 7 days plus current day
common_hallucinations: claiming driver must retain 14 days (driver: 7+current; carrier: 6 months)

questions.question: What is the difference between a malfunctioning ELD and a data diagnostic event?
key_concepts: diagnostic event: detected anomaly that doesn't prevent compliance
malfunction must be repaired within 8 days; if not, FMCSA extension required
drivers maintain paper RODS during malfunction
common_hallucinations: treating diagnostic events the same as malfunctions
claiming paper logs aren't allowed during ELD malfunction

questions.question: What is the general cargo securement requirement under Part 393 Subpart I?
key_concepts: secured by structures of adequate strength

questions.question: What is the minimum number of tiedowns required based on cargo length?
key_concepts: >10 ft: 2 plus 1 additional for each 10 ft increment beyond 10 ft

questions.question: What lighting and reflectors are required on a CMV under Part 393?
key_concepts: all required lamps in operable condition
conspicuity material (red/white retroreflective tape) on trailers
minimum requirements for headlamps, taillamps, brake lights, turn signals, marker lamps, identification lamps

questions.question: What is the regulation on use of mobile phones while driving a CMV?
key_concepts: no hand-held mobile phone use while operating CMV
includes reaching for, dialing, or pressing more than a single button
common_hallucinations: claiming all mobile phone use is banned (hands-free is allowed)

questions.question: What is the difference between FMCSA Operating Authority (MC number) and a USDOT number?
key_concepts: USDOT number: identifier for all interstate CMVs and intrastate hazmat
MC/MX/FF number: operating authority granted under Part 365
for-hire carriers transporting regulated commodities need both
private carriers and exempt commodities only need USDOT
common_hallucinations: claiming private carriers need MC numbers
